findings.costIfIgnored: A dead disk, a bad deploy or a deleted file wipes every customer, booking and deposit record, and the owner cannot say who has paid.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a nightly backup of salon.db to storage off the server (for example a copy to a cloud bucket), keep the last 14 copies, and add a short README section that says how to restore and has been tried once.
findings.plain: All customers, bookings and payment references live in one file, salon.db, on the same machine as the app. Nothing in the project copies it anywhere else.
findings.title: Booking data has no backup

findings.costIfIgnored: Someone can guess customer passwords all night, and a single script can make the app slow for everyone while it does.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a limit on POST /api/login and POST /api/register (for example 10 tries per address per 15 minutes, using the express-rate-limit package), return a clear 'Too many attempts, try again later' message, and add a test for it.
findings.plain: Anyone can try to sign in as fast as they like. There is no limit per address or per account.
findings.title: Nothing slows repeated sign-in attempts

findings.costIfIgnored: A bored visitor or a script can book every slot for weeks and the salon loses real customers without anyone being told why.
findings.fixPrompt: Make a booking that is still pending after 15 minutes release its slot (a scheduled clean-up or a check in the slots query), limit each account to 3 pending bookings, and add tests for both.
findings.plain: A new booking holds its time slot as soon as it is created, before any deposit is paid, and nothing ever releases it. Each slot can only be held once.
findings.title: Unpaid bookings hold slots forever

findings.costIfIgnored: A crash at night goes unnoticed until a customer phones the owner. The owner then has nothing to look at to find out when it broke or why.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a GET /health route that checks the database answers, add one central error handler that logs the route, the time and the error, and send those logs and a simple uptime check to a service that emails the owner when the app is down.
findings.plain: The app writes one line to the console when it starts and nothing else. There is no health check, no error report and no alert if it stops.
findings.title: The owner would not know the app is down

findings.costIfIgnored: The owner loses hours matching bank alerts to bookings by hand, and a customer who paid can be told their booking is not confirmed.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a payments log table that records every verify attempt (booking id, reference, result, time), add a Paystack webhook that confirms the booking if the customer's browser never calls verify, and show unmatched payments on the admin page.
findings.plain: If Paystack cannot be reached when the customer's browser asks to confirm a deposit, the booking stays pending and the customer is told to try again. Nothing records the attempt, and nothing confirms the booking later by itself.
findings.title: A customer who paid may not get a confirmed booking, and the owner cannot check

findings.costIfIgnored: Every restart or update signs all customers out in the middle of booking, and memory use grows with each visitor until the app stops.
findings.fixPrompt: Keep sessions in the database instead of memory (for example connect-sqlite3 or a session table), set the cookie to secure and httpOnly, and add a test that a session survives a restart.
findings.plain: Sign-in sessions are kept in the app's own memory, which the app clears on every restart and which grows with the number of visitors.
findings.title: Sessions are lost on restart and grow with visitors

findings.costIfIgnored: With ten times the customers, a rush of sign-ins at the same moment makes every page wait, including people who are already paying.
findings.fixPrompt: Replace bcrypt.hashSync and bcrypt.compareSync in the register and login routes with the async versions (bcrypt.hash and bcrypt.compare) and add a test that two sign-ins at once both complete.
findings.plain: Checking a password takes a fraction of a second during which the whole app stands still and serves nobody else. Today that is invisible. With many sign-ins at once, everyone queues behind each other.
findings.title: Many sign-ins at once would freeze the app

findings.costIfIgnored: A mistyped or missing payment key in production quietly turns the shop into one that confirms bookings without taking any money, and nobody sees it.
findings.fixPrompt: Make the app refuse to start when NODE_ENV is production and the Paystack keys or SESSION_SECRET are missing, keep the no-payment demo mode only when NODE_ENV is not production, and stop printing the seeded admin password to the console.
findings.plain: When the Paystack secret key is missing, the app confirms bookings without any payment and says nothing to the owner. The admin account is also seeded with a default password that is printed to the console on first start.
findings.title: A missing payment key confirms bookings for free
